title: NSGo game editor agent automations (version 1)
description:
AutomationsFile holds a project's shared agent automations in versioned YAML (automations.yaml beside game.yaml). A file looks like this:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://game.nsgo.dev/schemas/automations.v1.json version: 1 automations: - id: level-check name: A level file changes enabled: true trigger: event: file_changed glob: scenes/level_*.scene.yaml instruction: runs game check and 5 playtests, reports only problems

ParseAutomations decodes it strictly and EncodeAutomations writes it back in canonical form, so a file EncodeAutomations wrote survives a load and save byte for byte.

version.description: Version is the schema version; it must equal AutomationsVersion (1).

automations.description: Automations lists the project's configured automations in display order.

AutomationRule.description: AutomationRule defines one WHEN -> THE AGENT automation entry in automations.yaml.

id.description: ID uniquely identifies the automation inside automations.yaml (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores).

name.description: Name is the short human-readable WHEN summary shown in Settings › Automations. When omitted, the editor derives one from Trigger.

enabled.description: Enabled controls whether the automation is active.

trigger.description: Trigger defines the event that starts the automation.

instruction.description: Instruction is the work the agent performs when Trigger fires; its result always lands in Ready to review.

AutomationTrigger.description: AutomationTrigger describes when an automation starts.

event.description: Event selects the trigger event ("file_changed", "review_kept", "file_added", "before_export", or "daily").

glob.description: Glob matches slash-separated project-relative file paths using *, **, and ?. Required for file_changed and optional for review_kept and file_added.

kind.description: Kind selects the kind of added file for file_added triggers ("prefab", "scene", "tileset", "cutscene", "material", "particles", "rig", "screen", "datatable", "script", "asset", or "any").

platform.description: Platform optionally restricts before_export triggers to a target platform such as "ios", "android", "web", "macos", "windows", or "linux".

time.description: Time is the 24-hour local clock time ("HH:MM") when a daily trigger runs while the editor is open.
